Current evidence freshness

Sequential assessment 2026-09-12: retain P1 release assurance. Current docs/release-report.json is dated 2026-08-24, names 7b97d69d9d15241fad9cf6d41d85382ebc7bad4c, release_eligible=false, all six local gates not_run, and three external evidence slots unverified. Historical notes describing all-pass courts are not this checked-in report and must not be read as current qualification. Existing release driver/checks are present, so recover/refresh evidence rather than reimplement infrastructure. At release time run the complete gate set against the exact clean candidate, with source/fixture/provider hashes and bounded JVM/JS test batches as required by AGENTS.md; compare benchmark inputs and retain any discrepancies. Recent worktree scalafimCompileAll success and focused tests do not cover full release, coverage, docs, benchmarks or external evidence. Do not commit unrelated work merely to satisfy the clean-source guard. This assessment is local source/report review, not a fresh remote CI or branch-protection check; external state remains unverified until inspected.

Retained release acceptance

Scope

Close the epic only with reproducible performance and user-facing proof, while keeping correctness and noisy wall-clock benchmarking in separate lanes.

Acceptance criteria

- [ ] HRF convolution/integration JMH benchmarks cover the new structural/basis paths against retained baselines with source, runtime, platform, and parameter receipts.
- [ ] Fit benchmarks exercise factorization reuse, multiresponse throughput, chunking, WLS/GLS, and realistic predictor/response shapes.
- [ ] Allocation/work budgets target demonstrated hot paths and distinguish one-time planning from per-response/per-chunk cost.
- [ ] Performance regressions are evaluated in a dedicated benchmark lane and never cause numerical correctness tolerances to be weakened.
- [ ] Public first-level documentation explains the staged types, policy choices, structural design inspection, and basis-aware hypotheses.
- [ ] The DMS scenario is executable documentation and remains identical to its acceptance test construction.
- [ ] All documentation examples compile on the supported Scala version and identify pre-release limitations honestly.
- [ ] Fixture/manifest checks, focused JVM/Scala.js tests, compileAll, testAll, and any adopted formatting/compiler/coverage gates pass from a clean checkout.
- [ ] External reference disagreements and benchmark regressions are either resolved or recorded as explicit blocking caveats; no unexplained caveat passes release.
- [ ] A machine-readable final report links source commit, scenario receipts, toolchain versions, test results, and benchmark receipts.
